thread:
chris: Heads-up — starting a quick sweep for high-priv KMS bindings that appear ownerless or stale. Found a few in staging and one in prod that looks suspicious. kicking off triage and a small canary prune.

maya: +1. can you paste the prod binding id?

chris: prod-binding: projects/rw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/payments/cryptoKeys/backup_key -> role: roles/cloudkms.admin, bound to svcacct:svc-analytics@rw-prod. No owner tag in our inventory.

samir: ugh. svcacct looks like it was created by an old analytics job. I can take the owner lookup and call out any teams.

lena: if it's actually used by a cron, we need a graceful rollback plan. we should check last accessed and recent decrypt logs first.

chris: agreed. plan: 1) run KMS access query to collect last_access_time + principals; 2) try owner lookup via ownership-mapper; 3) run a staging canary prune (remove admin binding on staging keys) for 24h; 4) if no errors, schedule prod canary with oncall present and 1h rollback window.

devon: suggested query (gcloud + logging):
```
# list bindings
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy backup_key --project=rw-prod --format=json
# query audit logs
gcloud logging read "resource.type=crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName:Decrypt" --project=rw-prod --limit=100 
```
useful to pipe into jq to extract principals and timestamps.

samir: owner lookup result (quick): svc-analytics -> owner: unknown, last seen: 2024-11-02, provisioned by infra/jenkins-job-analytics-3. no active ticket.

maya: /cc @oncall — please be ready for prod canary tomorrow 10:30 PST if we decide to proceed. also i can run the staging prune this afternoon.

security-bot: automatic alert: key backup_key had Decrypt events 2 days ago (3 events). See link: https://console.logging/rw-prod/entries?query=backup_key

lena: 2 decrypts in 48h means we must be careful. can we identify the callers? service tokens?

chris: logging shows calls from svc-analytics and from an IP range used by batch-processing. samir is going to correlate with job schedules.

samir: correlation done — job runs nightly at 01:15 UTC, task name analytics/compute-export. likely legitimate but owner never claimed. I'll open a ticket to org-team and tag analytics@rw. ticket: SEC-1289.

devon: for automation, propose a small script for ownerbackfill-check:
```py
# scripts/ownerbackfill.py (sketch)
# 1) read kms binding list
# 2) lookup owner in ownership-db
# 3) if owner missing -> create draft PR to revoke admin role (staging only)
```
will add to infra repo and wire to nightly audit.

maya: timeline: staging prune today EOD, open ticket sent, prod canary hold until owner responds or we get explicit exemption. If no reply in 48h, escalate to product lead.

chris: thanks. one more ask: add an audit log hook to push KMS IAM diffs to the access-review dashboard so these show up in periodic recertification. low lift, high value.

devon: noted — I'll add a small CloudFunction to parse IAM change logs and emit to /recert/access.

security-bot: reminder: weekly recert run scheduled Fri 09:00 UTC — these items will be included once the dashboard hook is live.

maya: great. i'll update SEC-1289 with the staging run results and follow-ups. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
